pr_title: Fixes Market Simulated Automatic Option Assignment
pr_body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
* Add underlying holdings to regression result handler details log
> When debugging option exercise/assignment issues it's useful to see the
underlying holdings at the time the option contract fill event is processed.
> Also adds the full symbol string to the top of the order event section.
The Symbol.Value was being logged via OrderEvent.ToString(), but it wasn't
the full SecurityIdentifier - by including the full SID string it makes it
easier to correlate fills over symbol rename boundaries.

* Fix automatic option assignment from market simulation
> During the recent OptionExerciseOrder.Quantity refactor, this case was missed.
Additionally, it was realized that there were no regression tests covering the
automatic assignment via the market conditions simulation. This change introduces
a regression algorithm that covers the automatic assignment of put/call options.
#### Related Issue
<!--- This project only accepts pull requests related to open issues -->
<!--- If suggesting a new feature or change, please discuss it in an issue first -->
<!--- If fixing a bug, there should be an issue describing it with steps to reproduce -->
<!--- Please link to the issue here: -->
Fixes #4850 

#### Motivation and Context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
Simulated option assignment shouldn't act a fool

#### Requires Documentation Change
<!--- Please indicate if these changes will require updates to documentation, and if so, specify what changes are required -->
No.

#### How Has This Been Tested?
<!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your changes. -->
<!--- Include details of your testing environment, and the tests you ran to -->
<!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. -->
Added `OptionAssignmentRegressionAlgorithm` -- existing regression algorithms did not cover simulated assignment, only covering assignment at expiration. This new regression algorithm handles puts and calls.

issue_context.title: Simulated Option Assignment Orders Created With Wrong Sign
issue_context.body:
<!--- This template provides sections for bugs and features. Please delete any irrelevant sections before submitting -->

#### Expected Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the behavior you expect to see for your case. -->
Simulated option assignment orders reduce net exposure.

#### Actual Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the actual behavior for your case. -->
Simulated option assignment orders increase net exposure.

#### Potential Solution
<!--- Optional. Describe any potential solutions and/or thoughts as to what may be causing the difference between expected and actual behavior. -->
Fix sign in `BacktestingBrokerage.ActivateOptionAssignment`. Assignment takes place when we're short, therefore, assignment ALWAYS results in a positive order quantity to bring us to or closer to zero.

#### Reproducing the Problem
<!--- Required for Bugs. Describe how to reproduce the problem. This can be via a failing unit test or a simplified algorithm that reliably demonstrates this issue.  -->
The following algorithm showcases the issue. We write an AAPL put, taking a short position. This position gets auto-assigned via `BasicOptionAssignmentSimulation`. This is then piped through to `BacktestingBrokerage.ActivateOptionAssignment` where a `SubmitOrderRequest` gets generated with a negative order quantity.
<details>

``` csharp
public class OptionAssignmentRegressionAlgorithm : QCAlgorithm,
{
    Security Stock;
    Symbol PutOption = null;
    public override void Initialize()
    {
        SetStartDate(2020, 09, 14);
        SetEndDate(2020, 09, 15);
        SetCash(100000);
        Stock = AddEquity("SPY", Resolution.Minute);
        PutOption = OptionChainProvider.GetOptionContractList(Stock.Symbol, UtcTime)
            .Where(c => c.ID.OptionRight == OptionRight.Put)
            .Where(c => c.ID.Date == new DateTime(2020, 09, 18))
            .Single(c => c.ID.StrikePrice == 360m);
        AddOptionContract(PutOption);
    }
    public override void OnData(Slice data)
    {
        if (!Portfolio.Invested)
        {
            MarketOrder(PutOption, -1, tag:$"Open short position");
            Debug($"Sold 1 {PutOption.Value}");
        }
    }
    public override void OnOrderEvent(OrderEvent evt)
    {
    	var order = Transactions.GetOrderById(evt.OrderId);
    	Debug("ORDER: " + order);
    	Debug(" FILL: " + evt);
    	foreach (var kvp in Portfolio)
    	{
    		var symbol = kvp.Key;
    		var holding = kvp.Value;
    		Debug($"{symbol}:  {holding.Quantity}");
    	}
    }
    public override void OnAssignmentOrderEvent(OrderEvent evt)
    {
    	var order = Transactions.GetOrderById(evt.OrderId);
    	Debug("ORDER: " + order);
    	Debug(" FILL: " + evt);
    	foreach (var kvp in Portfolio)
    	{
    		var symbol = kvp.Key;
    		var holding = kvp.Value;
    		Debug($"{symbol}:  {holding.Quantity}");
    	}
    }
    public override void OnEndOfAlgorithm()
    {
        Debug($"PutOption.Value holding quantity = {Portfolio[PutOption].Quantity}");
        Debug($"Stock.Symbol.Value holding quantity = {Portfolio[Stock.Symbol].Quantity}");
    }
}
```

</details>
